paragraphs.heading: Study overview & computational workflow
paragraphs.purpose: Summarize the three-stage study workflow (data generation → VI selection → surrogate-based global sensitivity analysis) and enumerate input/output types and phenotype cases modeled.
must_not_claim: any results (e.g., which VI was selected), performance metrics of surrogates, or sensitivity outcomes

paragraphs.heading: Pulsatile FSI simulations
paragraphs.purpose: Describe the cost-effective pulsatile FSI pipeline used to generate time-resolved fluid and solid outputs for two idealized plaque phenotypes (LAP, CP), and state boundary-condition sources.
must_not_claim: that the FSI solver is novel or validated here (its development/validation is out of scope)

paragraphs.purpose: Provide finite-element discretization and time-integration details (element type/size, temporal resolution, convergence tolerances) and summarize mesh-independence checks that determined mesh choice.
must_not_claim: that discretization errors are negligible for all possible metrics beyond those reported; any result-level agreement with literature

paragraphs.heading: Input design-of-experiments and phenotype setup
paragraphs.purpose: Define the input parameter space (morphology, hemodynamics, material), sampling plan and case counts; describe phenotype-specific domain partitioning (LAP: 3 domains; CP: 4 domains) and uniform fibrous-cap thickness assumption.
must_not_claim: that the idealized geometries are equivalent to patient-specific anatomies or that FC thickness heterogeneity was modeled

paragraphs.heading: Stress metrics and postprocessing
paragraphs.purpose: Define PSS and ΔPSS calculations, the spherical/surface-averaged statistics used, and the rupture-location index computed from FSI outputs.
must_not_claim: any comparative superiority of ΔPSS versus PSS (this is a result/discussion claim)

paragraphs.heading: Vulnerability-index candidates and selection procedure
paragraphs.purpose: Specify the six candidate VI formulations (two stress measures × three strength-normalization exponents α), the seven pre-specified clinical sign criteria used for evaluation, and the filtering/selection workflow that yields final candidate(s).
must_not_claim: which candidates passed the criteria or any performance outcomes (these are Results)

paragraphs.heading: Surrogate modeling and Sobol global sensitivity analysis
paragraphs.purpose: Describe GPR surrogate training (kernel, ARD length-scales, hyperparameter tuning, normalization, fixed noise, 5-fold CV, implementation details), sample counts used to train models (valid pairs), and the Sobol estimation performed on surrogates (Monte Carlo sample size, group/individual indices computed).
must_not_claim: results of Sobol indices (e.g., that Material > Hemodynamics > Morphology) or surrogate numeric performance metrics (R², RMSE, coverage) which belong in Results

paragraphs.heading: Simulation outputs and validation
paragraphs.purpose: Report that the pulsatile FSI simulations produced time-resolved PSS fields, ΔPSS and rupture-location indices and that basic simulation outputs and mesh-independence behavior are consistent with prior studies and acceptable discretization error.
must_not_claim: Do not claim clinical predictive validity of simulation outputs against patient outcomes
Do not assert that the cost-effective FSI method is a novel contribution (tool only)

paragraphs.purpose: Summarize the computed stress metrics used for VI construction (surface-averaged PSS and ΔPSS), define ΔPSS operationally, and report that these quantities were extracted for all valid simulation cases.
must_not_claim: Do not present methodological details beyond results (e.g., solver internals or mesh convergence rationale)
Do not claim that ΔPSS necessarily causes rupture (only that it is a measured metric)

paragraphs.heading: Vulnerability-index candidate evaluation and selection
paragraphs.purpose: Report the evaluation of six candidate VIs (2 stress measures × 3 strength-normalizations) against seven pre-specified clinical sign criteria and state that two ΔPSS‑based indices (VI1 and VI2) satisfied all seven criteria.
must_not_claim: Do not claim that the selected VIs have been clinically validated against patient outcomes
Do not assert superiority of VI formulations beyond the specified sign-criteria evaluation

paragraphs.heading: Surrogate model performance
paragraphs.purpose: Present GPR surrogate training sample counts and cross-validation performance (R², RMSE) and calibration coverage for the selected VIs for both phenotypes to justify downstream sensitivity analysis.
must_not_claim: Do not claim surrogate models are perfect representations of FSI (acknowledge approximation)
Do not use surrogate performance to claim clinical utility

paragraphs.heading: Grouped Sobol sensitivity (Material vs Hemodynamics vs Morphology)
paragraphs.purpose: Report grouped Sobol first-order (S1) and total (ST) indices for Material, Hemodynamics and Morphology for both phenotypes and both selected VIs, and state that Material group explains the largest share of variance (Material > Hemodynamics > Morphology).
must_not_claim: Do not claim causal mechanisms linking inputs to rupture beyond variance contribution
Do not claim that grouped indices replace the need for individual-parameter analysis

paragraphs.purpose: Present individual-parameter Sobol S1 and ST indices, give the ranking of top drivers across phenotypes and VIs, and identify the four leading parameters (E_vessel, E_FC, SBP, PP).
must_not_claim: Do not overinterpret ranking as definitive in vivo causation
Do not claim that parameters not in the top four are unimportant in all contexts

paragraphs.heading: Interpretation of ΔPSS-based vulnerability indices
paragraphs.purpose: Explain why ΔPSS (stress amplitude) is a more appropriate stress metric than instantaneous peak PSS for vulnerability indices and link this to the need for pulsatile FSI.
must_not_claim: Do not claim clinical outcome prediction or proven causal mechanisms of rupture in patients.
Do not claim that instantaneous PSS is useless in all contexts.

paragraphs.purpose: Summarize the empirical evidence from candidate evaluation showing ΔPSS-based VIs outperform PSS-based candidates on the seven clinical sign criteria.
must_not_claim: Do not overstate generalizability to patient populations beyond the modeled phenotypes (no clinical validation).

paragraphs.heading: Role of material normalization (strength) in VI definition
paragraphs.purpose: Explain why normalizing stress by material strength (placing strength in the denominator) is necessary and how the normalization exponent α affects VI behavior and sensitivity.
must_not_claim: Do not claim a single universally optimal α for all plaque types beyond the two selected candidates.
Do not claim direct measurement protocols for strength are established clinically here.

paragraphs.purpose: Describe how variation of α changed candidate rankings and contributed to selecting VI1 and VI2, referencing the selection procedure and its outcomes.
must_not_claim: Do not claim that the two selected VIs (α=0.5,1.0) are definitive clinical standards without further validation.

paragraphs.heading: Dominance of material properties and implications for risk stratification
paragraphs.purpose: Interpret the Sobol sensitivity results showing material group dominance (Material > Hemodynamics > Morphology) and identify practical implications for prioritizing measurements.
must_not_claim: Do not claim that morphology or hemodynamics are unimportant in all clinical contexts.
Do not claim direct causation of rupture from the Sobol ranking alone.

paragraphs.purpose: Highlight the top individual drivers (E_vessel, E_FC, SBP, PP) from individual Sobol indices and discuss how this informs which measurements (e.g., stiffness assessment, blood pressure control) could most reduce VI uncertainty.
must_not_claim: Do not assert that intervention on these parameters will definitively prevent rupture without clinical trials.
Do not claim the surrogate-derived ranking is free of approximation error.

paragraphs.heading: Methodological considerations and limitations
paragraphs.purpose: Discuss methodological caveats: idealized geometries, uniform FC thickness, linear elastic materials, surrogate approximation, and that the cost-effective FSI tool is used as a means (not newly validated here).
must_not_claim: Do not claim that these limitations invalidate the qualitative ordering of parameter importance shown.
Do not claim methodological novelty or validation of the cost-effective FSI solver within this paper.

paragraphs.purpose: State practical recommendations for future work: need for patient-specific validation, spatially varying FC thickness and nonlinear/fatigue material models, and integration of stiffness measurement into imaging workflows.
must_not_claim: Do not claim that the recommendations have been tested or proven in clinical studies within this work.

paragraphs.heading: Clinical burden and motivation
paragraphs.purpose: State the public-health and clinical importance of coronary plaque rupture as the principal cause of acute coronary syndromes and its contribution to cardiovascular mortality, motivating improved rupture-risk metrics.
must_not_claim: Any new clinical prognostic utility or patient-outcome improvement from the present computational indicators (those are not validated here).
That the present models provide direct diagnostic rules for individual patients.

paragraphs.purpose: Briefly summarize the multivariate determinants of rupture risk (morphology, hemodynamics, material/strength) and emphasize that rupture arises from their interaction rather than any single factor.
must_not_claim: Quantitative dominance of any factor group (this paragraph only summarizes the multi-factorial nature; results come later).

paragraphs.heading: Limitations of existing vulnerability indices
paragraphs.purpose: Explain shortcomings of prior vulnerability indices: they are typically stress-only, assume fixed fibrous-cap strength across patients, and therefore may mischaracterize true rupture propensity.
must_not_claim: That all prior studies failed to consider material variability in any respect (avoid overgeneralization).
That prior stress-only indices are useless; instead present them as limited for the stated reasons.

paragraphs.purpose: Argue why pulse-resolved (pulsatile) simulations and strength-normalized risk metrics are necessary: ΔPSS captures fatigue/amplitude effects and strength should appear in the denominator of a VI; also note computational barriers that have prevented simultaneous wide-ranging sensitivity analysis across morphology, hemodynamics and material properties.
must_not_claim: That pulsatile simulations alone guarantee clinically validated risk prediction (validation is out of scope).
That computational barriers cannot be overcome by any method other than the pipeline used here (avoid exclusive claims).

paragraphs.heading: Objective and study approach
paragraphs.purpose: State the study objective: to evaluate ΔPSS-based, strength-normalized vulnerability indices and to determine which parameter groups dominate VI variance by combining a validated cost-effective pulsatile FSI pipeline, candidate VI selection against seven clinical criteria, GPR surrogates, and Sobol global sensitivity analysis across two plaque phenotypes.
must_not_claim: That this work validates the cost-effective FSI solver itself (its development/validation is prior work and out of scope).
That clinical outcome validation is performed in this study.

paragraphs.heading: Main findings
paragraphs.purpose: Concise restatement of the study's primary results: selected VI form, superiority of ΔPSS, and dominance of material properties in sensitivity analysis.
must_not_claim: That the selected VIs have been clinically validated against patient outcomes
That the surrogate replaces the need for any further high-fidelity FSI in all contexts

paragraphs.purpose: State practical implications: necessity of pulsatile simulations (ΔPSS interpretation), importance of normalizing by fibrous-cap strength (exponent α), and priority of material characterization for clinical risk stratification.
must_not_claim: That morphology measurements are unimportant in all clinical settings
That specific clinical measurement protocols (e.g. OCT procedures) are definitively recommended based solely on this study

paragraphs.heading: Methodological and translational notes
paragraphs.purpose: Summarize methodological strengths enabling the analysis (cost‑effective pulsatile FSI + GPR surrogates + Sobol sampling) and report surrogate performance and computational benefit to justify conclusions.
must_not_claim: That the cost-effective FSI solver's development/validation is a primary contribution of this paper

paragraphs.heading: Limitations and future work
paragraphs.purpose: Explicitly acknowledge study limitations (idealized geometries, uniform FC thickness, linear elasticity, surrogate approximation) and outline immediate future directions to address them.
must_not_claim: That these limitations invalidate the comparative sensitivity ranking reported here

paragraphs.heading: Data and ethical statements
paragraphs.purpose: Provide data availability and ethical declarations required by the journal (locate provided data files and state ethics where applicable).
must_not_claim: That patient data were used (no patient data were used in this computational study)
That specific ethical approval for human subjects was required or obtained if not applicable

paragraphs.purpose: Summarize the study's aim, methods, principal results, and main conclusions in a single unstructured abstract paragraph suitable for journal submission.
must_not_claim: Do not claim clinical validation against patient outcomes or prognostic utility beyond the reported sign-consistency tests.
Do not claim development or primary validation of the cost-effective FSI solver (treat solver as a referenced tool).
Do not assert causal relationships beyond variance attribution from Sobol indices (avoid clinical causation statements).
Do not report detailed methodological parameters best left to Methods (avoid over-detailed solver implementation beyond cited essentials).
